title: Sales and business development
short: Research accounts faster and send messages that are actually relevant.
why: Most selling time goes to research, writing and follow-up. AI can prepare drafts quickly, but the value comes from relevance and accuracy, which stay with you.

tasks.name: Account research brief
tasks.what: Turn public information into a one-page brief.

tasks.name: First-touch message
tasks.what: Draft a short message tied to a public signal.
tasks.check: Remove any claim you cannot source.

tasks.name: Follow-up that adds value
tasks.what: Add something useful instead of nagging.
tasks.check: Would you want to receive it?

tasks.name: Objection handling
tasks.what: Prepare honest answers to common objections.
tasks.check: Only claim what you can back up.

tasks.name: Call preparation
tasks.what: Goal, questions, likely objections, next step.

pilot: Pick 10 accounts you would contact this week anyway.
Use the brief and first-touch prompts for 5 of them. Do the other 5 as usual.
Compare time spent and reply quality after two weeks.
metrics: Reply rate and quality of replies
risks: Invented facts about a prospect
Over-personalised messages that feel invasive
Pasting private customer data into a consumer account

title: Marketing and growth
short: Turn one idea into many formats without losing accuracy or brand voice.
why: Content takes time to adapt for each channel. AI is useful for first drafts and variations. Strategy, claims and brand voice remain human decisions.

tasks.name: Release to post
tasks.what: Explain a product or industry change for your audience.
tasks.check: Link every claim to its source.

tasks.name: Headline variations
tasks.what: Generate options, then choose and test.

tasks.name: Repurpose an article
tasks.what: One article into email, posts and a script.

tasks.name: Audience questions
tasks.what: What your audience searches for at each stage.

tasks.name: Brand voice check
tasks.what: Flag lines that do not sound like you.

pilot: Choose one article you already published.
Create the email and three posts with the repurpose prompt.
Publish, then compare time spent and engagement with your usual process.
risks: Unsourced statistics
Generic copy that sounds like everyone else
Publishing without a fact check

title: Founders and business owners
short: Make decisions faster and find the repeated work worth simplifying.
why: You carry many decisions and a lot of repeated work. AI can structure your thinking and draft routine documents, but it cannot know your business context unless you provide it.

tasks.name: Compare two options
tasks.what: Structured trade-offs with assumptions stated.

tasks.name: Pre-mortem a plan
tasks.what: Imagine it failed and list the likely reasons.

tasks.name: Weekly update
tasks.what: Turn bullets into a clear update.

tasks.name: Write an SOP
tasks.what: Turn how you do it into steps.

tasks.name: Find repeated work
tasks.what: Spot what to simplify or automate.

pilot: List last week's tasks and run the repeated-work prompt.
Pick one repeated task and write its SOP.
Trial a draft-then-review routine for two weeks and measure time saved.
metrics: Hours saved on the chosen task
Cost of tools versus time saved
risks: Treating confident advice as fact
Sharing confidential financials or customer data
Automating a messy process

title: Students and teachers
short: Learn faster and practise better, while keeping the learning yours.
why: AI is good at explanations, practice and feedback when you stay active. It is a poor substitute for doing the thinking, and your school's rules come first.

tasks.name: Explain it simply
tasks.what: Plain-English explanation with an analogy.

tasks.name: Reading list
tasks.what: A week-by-week plan with checks.

tasks.name: Practice quiz
tasks.what: Questions and an answer key.

tasks.name: Study plan
tasks.what: A realistic day-by-day schedule.

tasks.name: Teach it back
tasks.what: Explain it and get feedback.

tasks.name: Lesson outline (teachers)
tasks.what: A structured lesson in minutes.

pilot: Choose one topic you find hard.
Use explain-simply, then teach-it-back, then a practice quiz.
Check answers against your notes and record what you got wrong.
risks: Submitting AI text as your own work against school rules
Learning a confident but wrong explanation
Skipping the effort that builds understanding

title: Creators and freelancers
short: Draft faster and keep your own voice and your clients' trust.
why: Creators and freelancers sell judgement and voice. AI can speed up structure and variations, while your taste and honesty are what clients pay for.

tasks.name: Tighten a draft
tasks.what: Cleaner version without changing meaning.

tasks.name: Sound more human
tasks.what: Shorter sentences, concrete examples.

tasks.name: Headline variations
tasks.what: Options grouped by approach.

tasks.name: Repurpose one piece
tasks.what: Multiple formats from one source.

tasks.name: Audience questions
tasks.what: What people want answered.
tasks.check: Pick the ones you can answer well.

pilot: Take one finished piece and repurpose it into three formats.
Time yourself against your normal process.
Ask a client or friend which version reads better.
metrics: How often you override the draft
risks: Losing your distinct voice
Disclosure rules about AI use with clients or platforms
Copying phrases too close to other work

title: Developers and IT
short: Understand, test and review code faster while a person stays accountable.
why: AI can explain code, draft tests and spot risks quickly. It can also be confidently wrong, so every suggestion needs running, reading and review.

tasks.name: Explain this code
tasks.what: Step-by-step plain-English explanation.

tasks.name: Write tests
tasks.what: Normal, edge and failure cases.

tasks.name: Review a change
tasks.what: Bugs, security, missing tests.

tasks.name: Debug from an error
tasks.what: Ranked causes and quick checks.
tasks.check: Understand before you apply a fix.

tasks.name: Extract structured data
tasks.what: Messy text into a table.

pilot: Pick one small, low-risk module.
Use explain, tests and review prompts on it.
Measure time to understand and the defects found, versus your usual process.
risks: Pasting secrets or proprietary code into a consumer account
Plausible but incorrect code
Over-trusting generated tests

title: HR and people teams
short: Draft clearer roles and fairer interviews while keeping people decisions human.
why: HR work mixes routine documents with sensitive decisions about people. AI can speed up drafting and structure, but fairness, privacy and final judgement stay with people.

tasks.name: Job description
tasks.what: Clear purpose, requirements and an honest note on difficulty.

tasks.name: Structured interview questions
tasks.what: Same questions, same scoring, for every candidate.
tasks.check: Review for fairness with your HR lead.

tasks.name: Meeting minutes
tasks.what: Turn notes into decisions and owners.

tasks.name: Write an SOP
tasks.what: Document a recurring HR process.
tasks.check: Walk it through with the process owner.

pilot: Pick one recurring document, such as job descriptions.
Draft three with the prompt and compare against your usual versions.
Have a colleague review for fairness and clarity before use.
risks: Biased or exclusionary wording
Pasting personal data about employees or candidates
Using AI output as the decision rather than as input

title: Finance and accounting
short: Explain numbers and chase invoices faster while every figure is checked by a person.
why: Finance teams spend time explaining numbers and writing routine messages. AI helps with wording and structure, but accuracy and approval are non-negotiable.

tasks.name: Variance commentary
tasks.what: Explain budget versus actual to non-finance readers.

tasks.name: Payment reminder
tasks.what: A firm, respectful follow-up for overdue invoices.

tasks.name: Compare two options
tasks.what: Structured trade-offs with stated assumptions.

tasks.name: Extract data from messy text
tasks.what: Turn text into a table, leaving gaps blank.

pilot: Choose one monthly commentary you write today.
Draft it with the prompt using anonymised or approved figures.
Compare time and accuracy; have a colleague check every number.
metrics: Number of figure errors caught in review
risks: Wrong or invented figures
Sharing confidential financials with a consumer account
Over-relying on a fluent explanation

title: Customer support
short: Draft consistent replies and help-centre content, with a person approving what customers see.
why: Support teams answer the same questions many times. AI can draft replies and macros quickly, while accuracy, tone and policy remain with trained staff.

tasks.name: Draft a support reply
tasks.what: Use only approved information; say what is unknown.

tasks.name: Summarise a ticket thread
tasks.what: Five-line summary with next step and owner.
tasks.check: Check for sensitive data before sharing.

tasks.name: Reusable macro
tasks.what: Turn a resolved ticket into a template.

tasks.name: Help-centre article
tasks.what: From a resolved issue to a clear article.

pilot: Pick your five most common questions.
Create approved macros and help articles with the prompts.
Measure handling time and reopened tickets for two weeks.
risks: Wrong policy statements sent to customers
Pasting customer personal data into a consumer account
Tone that does not match your brand

title: Operations and project teams
short: Find repeated work, document it, and keep status updates honest.
why: Operations teams run on documented processes and clear communication. AI can help draft SOPs and updates, but only the people doing the work can confirm what is true.

tasks.name: Find repeated work
tasks.what: Group last week's tasks and spot candidates to simplify.

tasks.name: Write a clear SOP
tasks.what: Turn how you do a task into steps.
tasks.check: Walk through it with someone who does the task.

tasks.name: Weekly status update
tasks.what: Progress, risks, decisions needed, next week.

tasks.name: Meeting minutes
tasks.what: Decisions, actions, open questions.

pilot: List last week's tasks and run the repeated-work prompt.
Write the SOP for the top candidate and test it with a colleague.
Compare time and errors for two weeks.
metrics: Hours saved on the chosen process
risks: Documenting a broken process as if it were good
Status updates that hide risk
Sharing confidential project data
